about.title: Concord Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Ten people died on Concord's streets in 2025, according to the most recent final crash records. Behind each of those counts is a family in Contra Costa County trying to figure out what comes next. Some of those losses happened along Clayton Road or Willow Pass Road; others on SR-242 or SR-4, the corridors that carry much of the city's daily traffic, with reported crashes tending to cluster on Tuesday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. Wrongful death claims are not only about collisions, though. A fall at a workplace, a defective product, or negligent care can all lead to the same kind of civil case. In California, the right to bring that case belongs first to a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children, and then to certain dependents or heirs. The claim is separate from any criminal charges, and it moves on its own timeline, generally two years from the date of death, with a shorter window when a public agency is involved. LawProactive is free to use. We listen, and then connect you with an independent attorney who handles wrongful death matters and works on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Concord Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits who may bring a wrongful death action, starting with a spouse or domestic partner and children, then certain dependents and heirs. The attorney you are connected with can explain where your family stands before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims in California must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a city, county, or state agency may be responsible. Getting connected sooner protects those options.

items.title: The full picture of loss
items.desc: Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. Network attorneys work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: The crash that killed my family member happened on SR-4 in Concord. Does that change anything?
items.answer: It can. If a state or local agency's road design, maintenance, or vehicle is part of the picture, California requires a formal claim to that agency on a much shorter timeline than the standard two years. An attorney can look at the collision report and tell you whether a government claim needs to be filed alongside the wrongful death case.

items.question: There is already a criminal case in Contra Costa County. Do we still need a civil claim?
items.answer: Yes, they are two different things. A criminal case is brought by the district attorney and is about punishment; it does not pay for funeral costs or lost support. A wrongful death action is a civil case your family brings, and it can move forward whether or not criminal charges are filed or result in a conviction.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm, and what does it cost to use?
items.answer: LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free connection service that matches Concord families with an independent personal injury attorney who handles wrongful death claims. There is no charge to reach out, and the attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they are paid only if your case results in a recovery.
